column5: Description
New users can create an account using full name, email, and password.
Registered users can log in using email and password.
Passwords are stored using hashing, not plain text.
The system supports Admin, Staff, and Customer roles.
The system uses JWT session tokens with configurable expiration, default 7 days.
Each email address can only be registered once.
Passwords must be at least 6 characters long.
One role can be assigned to many users, and each user has exactly one role.
New registered users are automatically assigned the Customer role.
Customer can browse events, select seats, make bookings, process payments, view own booking history, and cancel pending bookings.
Staff has all Customer permissions plus event management permissions.
Admin has all Staff permissions plus ability to view all bookings and manage system settings.
Description
Users can view all available events with title and category.
Users can filter events by category such as Movie, Concert, and Seminar.
Users can search events by entering keywords in the event title.
Users can view full event details including description and related showtimes.
Admin and Staff users can create new events with title, description, and category.
One category can contain many events, and each event belongs to exactly one category.
Every event must belong to exactly one category.
All events are visible to authenticated users.
Description
Admin or Staff can create showtimes linking an event to a venue with date/time and base price.
Users can view all available venues with name and location.
Each venue defines seats with row label, seat number, and seat type.
Seat types such as VIP, Standard, and Sofa Bed apply a price multiplier to the showtime base price.
Users can view all showtimes for a specific event.
One venue can have many seats, and each seat belongs to exactly one venue.
One seat type can be assigned to many seats, and each seat has exactly one seat type.
One event can have many showtimes, and each showtime links to exactly one event.
One venue can host many showtimes, and each showtime is held at exactly one venue.
The booking transaction validates that the selected seat belongs to the same venue as the referenced showtime before inserting a BookingDetail.
Each seat type price modifier must be greater than zero.
Seat Price = Showtime Base Price x Seat Type Price Modifier.
Description
Users can create a booking containing one or more seats for a specific showtime.
A single booking can include multiple seats.
Users can view their own booking history ordered by most recent.
Each booking displays event name, showtime, seats, total amount, and status.
Users can cancel bookings that are in Pending status.
One user can have many bookings, and each booking belongs to exactly one user.
One status can be applied to many bookings, and each booking has exactly one status at a time.
One booking can contain many booking details, and each detail belongs to exactly one booking.
One showtime can have many booking details, and each detail references exactly one showtime.
One seat can appear in many booking details across different showtimes, and each detail references exactly one seat.
Booking expiration time must be after booking creation time.
Total booking amount must be non-negative.
Booking Total = Sum of all individual seat prices.
Bookings transition from Pending to Completed on payment or Cancelled by user.
Only Pending bookings can be cancelled by the user.
Cancelled bookings are preserved in the database and updated by status instead of being physically deleted.
Description
The system verifies seat availability before creating a booking.
If any requested seat is already booked, the entire booking request fails.
The seat map visually indicates which seats are already booked.
The system maintains a view of all seats per showtime with availability status and calculated seat price.
Before inserting booking details, the transaction validates that the selected seat belongs to the same venue as the referenced showtime.
A seat is unavailable if a BookingDetail exists for the same showtime and is linked to a Completed booking or an unexpired Pending booking.
Cancelled bookings and expired pending bookings release seats back to available.
If any requested seat is unavailable during transactional recheck, the entire booking request fails.
Seat availability and pricing are queried from the ShowtimeAvailableSeats view filtered by ShowtimeID.
Before inserting booking details, the system rechecks active bookings for the same ShowtimeID and SeatID within a transaction.
Description
All bookings are created with expiration time 15 minutes after creation.
The system rejects payment attempts for expired bookings.
On successful payment, booking status changes from Pending to Completed.
Users cannot create a new booking if the showtime StartDateTime has already passed.
Expired pending bookings are treated as inactive so their seats become available again.
ExpiresAt = NOW() + 15 minutes.
Pending bookings whose ExpiresAt has passed are inactive for seat availability and cannot be paid.
Description
Users can select from available payment methods such as PromptPay, Credit Card, TrueMoney, and ShopeePay.
The system creates a payment record with status, transaction ID, and amount.
A unique transaction ID is auto-generated for each payment.
Each booking has exactly one payment record.
The system records the exact timestamp of successful payment.
Each booking has at most one payment record, and each payment links to exactly one booking.
One payment method can be used in many payments, and each payment uses exactly one method.
One status can be applied to many payments, and each payment has exactly one status at a time.
Payment amount must be non-negative.
The system only allows payment methods that are currently active.
Each payment has a unique TransactionID.
Only the booking owner can process payment.
Description
One ticket is generated per seat in a completed booking.
Each ticket has a unique ticket number.
Each ticket displays event name, venue, showtime, seat info, and price.
Tickets can be verified by ticket number without authentication.
Users can view all tickets from their bookings.
Each booking detail generates exactly one ticket, and each ticket corresponds to exactly one booking detail.
Final ticket price must be non-negative.

The system displays all seats for a venue grouped by row with seat numbers.

Booked seats are visually distinguished from available seats.
Users can click seats to select and deselect them.
The system displays the running total of selected seats.
Description
Admin can analyze how total revenue for each event category changes month to month.
Admin can analyze seat zones where customers consistently prefer to sit.
Admin can analyze how quickly the platform expands month to month.
Admin can analyze how total revenue for each venue changes month to month.
Admin can analyze total bookings during each hour of the day.
Admin can compare sold tickets with total venue capacity for each showtime.

Description
Every table has a single-column auto-incrementing integer primary key.
All foreign keys are NOT NULL and include explicit ON DELETE behavior.
Users.RoleID references Roles.RoleID with SET DEFAULT behavior.
Events.CategoryID references EventCategories.CategoryID with RESTRICT behavior.
Seats.VenueID references Venues.VenueID with CASCADE behavior.
Seats.SeatTypeID references SeatTypes.SeatTypeID with RESTRICT behavior.
Showtimes.EventID references Events.EventID with CASCADE behavior.
Showtimes.VenueID references Venues.VenueID with RESTRICT behavior.
Bookings.UserID references Users.UserID with RESTRICT behavior.
Bookings.StatusID references BookingStatuses.StatusID with RESTRICT behavior.
BookingDetails.BookingID references Bookings.BookingID with RESTRICT behavior.
BookingDetails.ShowtimeID references Showtimes.ShowtimeID with RESTRICT behavior.
BookingDetails.SeatID references Seats.SeatID with RESTRICT behavior.
Payments.BookingID references Bookings.BookingID with RESTRICT behavior.
Payments.MethodID references PaymentMethods.MethodID with RESTRICT behavior.
Payments.StatusID references PaymentStatuses.StatusID with RESTRICT behavior.
Tickets.DetailID references BookingDetails.DetailID with RESTRICT behavior.
Booking, payment, and ticket data are preserved for history, reporting, and verification.
Users.Email prevents duplicate user accounts.
Payments.BookingID enforces one payment per booking.
Payments.TransactionID enforces unique gateway references.
Tickets.TicketNo enforces unique ticket verification codes.
Tickets.DetailID enforces one ticket per booking detail.
Seats has UNIQUE (VenueID, RowLabel, SeatNumber) to prevent duplicate seat positions within a venue.
Bookings.TotalAmount must be greater than or equal to 0.
Bookings.ExpiresAt must be greater than BookingTimestamp.
Payments.Amount must be greater than or equal to 0.
Showtimes.BasePrice must be greater than or equal to 0.
SeatTypes.PriceModifier must be greater than 0.
Tickets.FinalPrice must be greater than or equal to 0.
All tables include CreatedAt with default NOW().
All tables include UpdatedAt with auto-updated NOW().
Bookings.BookingTimestamp defaults to NOW().
PaymentMethods.IsActive defaults to TRUE.
Bookings.StatusID defaults to Pending.
Payments.StatusID defaults to Pending.
Users.RoleID defaults to Customer.
Users requires FullName, Email, Password, and RoleID.
Events requires CategoryID and Title.
Seats requires VenueID, SeatTypeID, RowLabel, and SeatNumber.
Showtimes requires EventID, VenueID, StartDateTime, and BasePrice.
Bookings requires UserID, StatusID, and ExpiresAt.
BookingDetails requires BookingID, ShowtimeID, and SeatID.
Payments requires BookingID, MethodID, and StatusID.
Tickets requires DetailID.
Description
The view displays all seats per showtime with availability status and calculated seat price.
A seat is unavailable when linked to a Completed booking or an unexpired Pending booking.
The view is used for querying and seat-map display.
Final double-booking prevention is enforced by transactional booking logic that rechecks active non-expired bookings for the same ShowtimeID and SeatID before insert.

Stores role-based access control information.
Stores registered user account information and credentials.
Stores categories for events.
Stores details of available events.
Stores physical venue information.
Stores event schedules linked to venues.
Stores seat types and pricing modifiers.
Stores seats mapped to venues.
Stores booking lifecycle statuses.
Stores user booking transactions.
Stores individual reserved seats for each booking.
Stores generated tickets for completed bookings.
Stores supported payment gateways and methods.
Stores payment transaction statuses.
Stores payment transaction records linked to bookings.
